title: Etale local linearization of a contracted smooth group curve
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Put $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units and $\mathbf G_{a,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[x]$ with addition. For a smooth group $H/S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], write $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\ker(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A))$, with addition from multiplication and scalar action from $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. Let $U/S$ be a smooth affine group of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with an action $a$ of $\mathbf G_{m,S}$ by group automorphisms. Assume every geometric fibre is isomorphic as a group to $\mathbf G_a$, and for every $A$-algebra $B$ and $u\in U(B)$ the orbit map $t\mapsto a(t,u)$ extends to $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]\to U_B$ with value $1_U$ at zero. Suppose $\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ is locally free of rank one and the differentiated coaction is $v\mapsto v\otimes t^n$ for a fixed integer $n>0$. Then there is a jointly surjective family of affine etale maps $S_i\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and group-scheme isomorphisms
$$q_i:\mathbf G_{a,S_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{S_i},\qquad q_i(t^nx)=a(t,q_i(x))$$
after every $S_i$-algebra extension. No invertibility of $n$ in $A$, reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $A$, or chosen section of $U$ away from its identity is required.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 4.2.2 and its proof, printed pp.117-119, with the preceding etale-local choice of a section away from the identity, printed p.117; extracted for a general contracted smooth curve with the same hypotheses used in that proof. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative algebraic-group theorem.

proof.text: First make the tangent comparison valid over arbitrary $A$. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with augmentation $e:C\to A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] and [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $\Omega_{C/A}$ is finite projective. Thus $Q=A\otimes_{C,e}\Omega_{C/A}$ is finite projective: tensor an inclusion and retraction exhibiting $\Omega_{C/A}$ as a summand of $C^N$. A tangent point with values in an $A$-algebra $B$ is exactly $c\mapsto e(c)+\epsilon D(c)$, where $D(cc')=e(c)D(c')+e(c')D(c)$ and $D(A)=0$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] identifies these points with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,B)$. The two unit identities for the comultiplication give addition of the two first-order coefficients; replacing $\epsilon$ by $b\epsilon$ gives scalar multiplication. These are precisely the operations used in the item.

source.place: Background on Lie functors, printed p.2; explicit affine tangent calculation supplementing the geometric-fibre weight comparison on printed pp.116–118; Stacks Tags 01V6, 02H6 and 00RO.

proof.text: For every $A$-algebra $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] identifies the cotangent module of $U_B$ at its identity with $B\otimes_A Q$. Since $Q$ is a summand of $A^N$, the comparison $B\otimes_A Q^*\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,B)$ is an isomorphism: it is the coordinate isomorphism for $A^N$, restricted by the same idempotent. This gives $\operatorname{Lie}(U_B)=B\otimes_A\operatorname{Lie}(U)$. The formulas $c\mapsto e(c)+\epsilon D(c)$ commute with the action morphism, so this comparison respects its coaction. Consequently the tangent action after every base change, in particular every geometric fibre, has weight $n$. This uses the entire character $t^n$, not the integer $n$ acting on a Lie algebra by multiplication.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, proof, printed p.118, identifying the fibre action exponent from the Lie action; tangent base change written out from Stacks Tag 00RV.

proof.text: Over an algebraically closed field $k$ above $S$, choose the given group isomorphism $U_k\simeq\mathbf G_{a,k}$. Its action is a polynomial $P(t,x)\in k[t,t^{-1}][x]$. The action by $t^{-1}$ is its polynomial inverse and the identity is fixed. Degrees in $x$ multiply over the domain $k[t,t^{-1}]$, so $P(t,x)=c(t)x$ with $c(t)$ a Laurent unit. A Laurent unit over a field has one nonzero term, so $c(t)=d t^m$ for an integer $m$; $P(1,x)=x$ gives $d=1$. Its tangent action is the character $t^m$, hence step 2 and independence of Laurent monomials give $m=n$. Thus on every geometric fibre the action is $t.x=t^n x$, with equality of group-scheme actions, including on points over nonreduced $k$-algebras.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.1.4 and Lemma 4.2.2, printed pp.116–118: classification of the action on each geometric additive fibre; polynomial-degree argument written out.

proof.text: The affine morphism $U\to S$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], so its identity section is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. Let $V=U\setminus e(S)$. It is smooth over $S$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], and surjective because every geometric fibre is $\mathbf A^1$ minus its origin. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to $V\to S$ (schemes are the special case of algebraic spaces) and refine the covering schemes by affine opens. This gives a jointly surjective family of affine etale $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to S$ with sections $\sigma_i$ of $U_{S_i}$ disjoint from its identity. Smoothness persists by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and a finite algebra presentation base changes by extending its coefficients. All action, contraction and tangent hypotheses persist: for contraction an $R_i$-algebra is already an $A$-algebra, and for tangent weights use step 2. Work on one such base $R$ and omit $i$. If $S$ is empty, use the empty family.

source.place: Preceding etale-local choice of a nonidentity section, printed p.117; Stacks Tags 01KT, 01VC, 01VA, 055U and 0CFV.

proof.text: The contraction hypothesis applied to $\sigma\in U(R)$ gives $q:\mathbf A^1_R\to U_R$ with $q(1)=\sigma$ and $q(0)=e$. It is equivariant for ordinary scaling on its source: the equality $q(tz)=a(t,q(z))$ holds for invertible $z$ by the action identity, and hence holds in general. Indeed both pullbacks of each coordinate function belong to $R[t,t^{-1},z]$, which injects into its localization at $z$, so their equality after localization implies equality. The same injection $R[z]\hookrightarrow R[z,z^{-1}]$ proves uniqueness of the extension and compatibility with base change. On a geometric fibre, use step 3 and normalize the additive coordinate to carry $\sigma$ to $1$. Then $q_k(z)=z^n$.

Apply [lem-sfb-mu-n-fixed-subgroup-smooth] to $U_R$ and its action, obtaining the smooth finitely presented closed fixed subgroup $F=U_R^{\mu_n}$. Formation of $F$ commutes with geometric base change. Step 3 shows $F_k=(U_R)_k$ on every geometric fibre, since $v^n=1$ makes $v^n x=x$ as a scheme-theoretic identity. The inclusion $F\to U_R$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence]: its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is finitely presented and $U_R$ is finitely presented. Its source is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Thus [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion], isomorphism clause, gives $F=U_R$. In particular the full group scheme $\mu_n$, including its infinitesimal points, acts trivially on $U_R$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, proof, printed p.118, mu_n-triviality; Conrad Lemma B.3.1 replaced by its existing Stacks geometric-fibre criterion node (Tags 039E, 02GM, 025G).

proof.text: It follows from equivariance that $q(vz)=q(z)$ for every $v\in\mu_n$. Write a coordinate pullback $q^*(c)=\sum_{j\geq0}b_jz^j$. In $R[z,v]/(v^n-1)$ invariance says $\sum_j b_jz^j(v^j-1)=0$. The basis $1,v,\ldots,v^{n-1}$ gives $b_j=0$ unless $n\mid j$; this is valid even if $n=0$ in $R$. Hence $q^*(c)$ lies in the subring $R[z^n]$. The injective map $R[w]\to R[z]$, $w\mapsto z^n$, therefore gives a unique algebra map $\bar q^*:C_R\to R[w]$ with $q^*(c)=\bar q^*(c)(z^n)$, and thus $\bar q:\mathbf A^1_R\to U_R$. The identical coefficient substitution in $R[t,t^{-1},w]$ shows $\bar q(t^n w)=a(t,\bar q(w))$; also $\bar q(0)=e$. No assertion about geometric points alone was used to factor $q$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, proof, printed p.118, categorical quotient by mu_n; the invariant-polynomial coefficient calculation is written out.

proof.text: On every geometric fibre $q_k(z)=z^n$ in the normalized coordinate of step 5. Injectivity of $k[w]\to k[z]$ gives $\bar q_k(w)=w$, so $\bar q_k$ is an isomorphism. Its source $\mathbf A^1_R$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], thus flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Its target $U_R$ is finitely presented. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence], $\bar q$ is locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] again to conclude that $\bar q$ is an isomorphism of $R$-schemes.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2, proof, printed p.118, fibral isomorphism criterion; Stacks Tags 00T7, 039E, 02GM, 025G.

proof.text: Transfer multiplication along $\bar q$ to a polynomial $m(x,y)\in R[x,y]$. The identity and equivariance give $m(x,0)=x$, $m(0,y)=y$ and $m(t^n x,t^n y)=t^n m(x,y)$ in $R[t,t^{-1},x,y]$. If $b_{ij}x^iy^j$ is a term, its two $t$-exponents are $n(i+j)$ and $n$. Since $n>0$, they are distinct integers unless $i+j=1$, so Laurent coefficient comparison kills all other terms over any $R$. Hence $m=cx+dy$, and the two unit identities give $c=d=1$. Thus $\bar q$ respects multiplication and the identity; it respects inverse as well because a multiplicative map sends the inverse to the unique inverse. Set $q_i=\bar q$ on each cover. The polynomial equivariance identity from step 7 remains true after every $R_i$-algebra extension, giving exactly the group-scheme isomorphisms and functorial identity required.

Step 1: the smooth-ring-map comparison and Kähler differentials give finite projective Q. Step 2: Lie commutes with every base change and keeps weight n, without the Noetherian tangent node. Step 3: composing with the inverse forces x-degree 1, and the Laurent unit with tangent weight n gives the action t^n x on every geometric fibre, scheme-theoretically. Step 4: separated affine morphism, so the identity section is closed and its complement V is smooth and surjective; lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections gives affine étale charts with a section σ; base change by lem-pc-proper-base-change(2). Step 5: the orbit map of σ extends, injectivity into the localization at z gives equivariance, and q_k(z)=z^n. Step 6: the new node's F is smooth fp; lem-pc-smooth-flat, lfp-permanence and the fibre isomorphism criterion (hypotheses match: X flat lfp, Y lft, f lfp) give F=U_R, which is valid over a nonreduced base. Step 7: the basis of R[v]/(v^n-1) puts q^* into R[z^n], giving the factorization q̄ with weight-n equivariance. Step 8: A^1 is smooth and the fibre criterion makes q̄ an isomorphism, also when the characteristic divides n. Step 9: exponent comparison with n>0 gives m=x+y. New node: true (fixed points of the multiplicative-type, finite locally free μ_n on a smooth separated affine group form a smooth closed subgroup; base change is formal). Edge cases n=1, n=p in char p, trivial action and the zero ring all hold. It is self-contained with three search kinds and does not restate an item clause.
